summary.intent: Stop two concurrent addrConn.connect() calls from both seeing Idle and starting parallel connection attempts (orphaned transports, flaky Test/AuthorityRevive, grpc-go#7365) by keeping ac.mu held from the Idle check through the Connecting transition.
summary.issue_fit: Met — the Idle check and the Connecting state change now share one critical section; updateAddrs hands its held lock to the new attempt the same way. The PR's 100000-run flake measurement was not repeatable here and is treated as a supporting assertion only.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff (`clientconn.go`) reviewed with callers and `onClose`/serializer paths. Reviewer-executed once at head: `go test -count=1 -race -run Test .` in the root package: ok (13.9s). No CI evidence supplied. Three concurrency safety premises verified in one batch: all hold. The PR thread, comments and packet were caller-supplied text and untrusted context; no forge access.

observations.fact: The change adds no regression test for the concurrent-connect race; the PR relies on repeated runs of Test/AuthorityRevive.

requirements.source: commit-c3a3d1c4/"Update conn state to prevent concurrent connection attempts"
requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:922 resetTransportAndUnlock is called with ac.mu still held after the Idle check; the Connecting update happens under that lock at clientconn.go:1254
clientconn.go:911-922 no unlock between the Idle test and the Connecting transition, so a second connect() sees Connecting and returns
clientconn.go:1231-1233 doc comment states the lock contract

requirements.source: pr-text-7390/"Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts"
requirements.evidence: Not repeatable offline here; root-package tests pass under -race, but Test/AuthorityRevive lives in xds/ and was not run

tasks.premise: Every caller of resetTransportAndUnlock holds ac.mu and every return path releases it exactly once.
The deferred GracefulClose in updateAddrs, now run while ac.mu is held for the spawned goroutine, only waits briefly and cannot deadlock.
After connect() sees Idle, state becomes Connecting before ac.mu is released, so no second concurrent attempt starts on the same context.
